correctness.rationale: The specified edge set has 12 degree-four vertices and 24 edges and is independently isomorphic to the Chvátal graph. Two bijective exhaustive enumerations—base-three words and zero-color subsets plus binary assignments on the complement—each cover all 3^12=531441 labeled configurations exactly once. Both agree on the full 13-sector minimum-energy and minimizing-count table and each of 24 unique-bond frustration counts. Rational convexity of the 12 successive integer minima differences (-1,-1,-1,0,0,1,3,3,4,4,4,4) proves all real-field branches and crossings without numerical extrapolation. Standalone verifier reruns every integer test, convex interval and exact degeneracy sum; proof concerns a finite system only.

value.rationale: The twelve-vertex Chvátal graph is the smallest triangle-free four-regular graph of chromatic number four, a canonical minimal frustrated antiferromagnet with three Potts states. The complete one-color field staircase, coexistence degeneracies and precise allowed locations of its unavoidable single bad bond form a natural graph-specific microcanonical/magnetic benchmark. The field envelope is not dictated by chromaticity or regularity; exact bond support reveals spatial heterogeneity hidden by uniform degrees. The motivation and scope are intrinsic to this graph and model, and no thermodynamic/large-scale significance is claimed.
